concept.title: Example Concept Topic
concept.shortdesc: An example DITA topic of type concept. This is a shared topic.

change-item.change-summary: This is a shared topic. If you change it, you change it for everyone. This is a part of the change-historylist which is part of the metadata of the topic. It is not included in the output. It allows for file history to be stored in the file. You can use this manually as a way to log changes, or you could write scripts that automagically populate this information.

conbody.p: This is a topic of type concept.
Concept topics are very similar to topic type topics. A concept does not have a lot of structure to it.
Concepts are intended for more free-form text, with illustrations, etc.

section.title: Sections
section.p: Concepts can have sections. However, once you start a section, you cannot return to the main body of the concept.

While sections may seem like just adding a sub-heading, by default, section titles are not included in the table of contents. They can be useful for grouping concepts, highlighting ideas, etc. If you add an id attribute to the section element, you can link to it, and the title of the section is automatically pulled in by the xref.

example.title: Section Specialization: Example
example.p: An example is just a fancy section. However, it does add the semantic idea of "this is an example" around the contents.
